name: Rebuttal paragraph on the split leakage

content.text: neurips D&B rebuttal for IDETrace. we found a leakage bug after submission (7/24): windows from the same student were in both train and test. fixed with group split by student id. macro-F1 went 0.81 -> 0.74. reviewer 2 asked about "possible overfitting to individual students". i want to be upfront. draft the paragraph, ~150 words, no groveling

**On overfitting to individual students (R2).** We thank R2 for this question, which led us to re-examine our evaluation. Our original split assigned windows to train and test at random, so windows from the same student could appear in both. This lets a model exploit student-specific patterns and overstates generalization. We re-ran all baselines with a split grouped by student ID, so no student appears in more than one partition. Macro-F1 for our best model changes from 0.81 to 0.74; the ranking of baselines is unchanged. We will report the grouped-split results as the main numbers, keep the original numbers in the appendix with an explanation, and release the split files so others can reproduce both. We believe the grouped split is the right default for this dataset and will state it as part of the benchmark protocol.

(~145 words)
is "ranking unchanged" true? let me check... yes all 4 baselines same order. but the gap between ours and the best baseline shrank from .09 to .05

Then say so, otherwise a reviewer who checks the appendix will feel misled. Replace the sentence with:

> Macro-F1 for our best model changes from 0.81 to 0.74; the ranking of all four baselines is unchanged, though the margin over the strongest baseline narrows from 0.09 to 0.05.

It costs you a little but reads as fully transparent, which is what you want in a rebuttal that's already admitting a bug.
should we also mention it in the general response to all reviewers

Yes, briefly. A reviewer who only reads the general response should not learn about a changed headline number from someone else's thread. Two sentences in the general response: what changed and why, plus "details in our response to R2." Keep the full explanation in one place so the numbers don't drift between versions.
Good luck. One last check before posting: make sure every place the paper's numbers appear in the rebuttal (general response, R2, any tables) uses the grouped-split values consistently.
